claim: Gorissen, Dhaene & De Turck (JMLR 2009) use a Genetic Algorithm to evolve a heterogeneous population spanning genuinely distinct surrogate model classes (SVM, Kriging, RBF, Neural Networks) that compete on approximation accuracy, but the GA here is the surrogate MODEL-SELECTION mechanism itself, not a black-box optimizer that searches the design/decision-variable space using the winning surrogate.
stance_target: Gorissen 2009 as a candidate KILL of N6 (surrogate class is varied, but no independently-crossed optimizer routine over the black-box design problem exists)
scope_conditions: global surrogate modeling for expensive simulation codes, JMLR 2009
quoted_support: Different model types are evolved cooperatively using a Genetic Algorithm (heterogeneous evolution) and compete to approximate the iteratively selected data. In this way the optimal model type and complexity for a given data set or simulation code can be dynamically determined.

claim: The paper's only other mention of an 'optimization algorithm' (BFGS, PSO, GA, DIRECT, NSGA-II) refers to fitting each surrogate candidate's own internal hyperparameters (e.g. kernel widths), not to a downstream black-box optimizer searching the design space using the fitted surrogate -- confirming this paper never crosses surrogate class with a decision-space optimizer.
stance_target: Gorissen 2009 as a candidate KILL of N6
quoted_support: a chosen hyperparameter optimization algorithm (e.g., BFGS, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), DIRECT, NSGA-II, etc.). Models are assigned a score based on one or more criteria.

claim: A full-text grep of the complete 40-page JMLR paper for factorial, crossed, ANOVA, analysis of variance, eta-squared, main effect, interaction, variance decomposition, and two-way returned zero hits, confirming no crossed factorial variance decomposition of surrogate class x optimizer exists in this paper.
stance_target: N6: no prior work runs a crossed surrogate x optimizer factorial with variance decomposition in this literature
quoted_support: Zero hits for: factorial, crossed, ANOVA, analysis of variance, eta squared, main effect, interaction, variance decomposition, two-way.
